reasoning: The observation is exact and the root cause is confirmed harder than the finding proved it: raising the single-population gate from 150 to 300 converts 5 of the 8 zero teams to 6-10 suggestions with no other change, which isolates BOARD_TOP_N_FILTER (src/trade/suggestions.py:239, applied at :650-651 in build_asset_pool_from_contract) as the cause. I confirmed both render in a real browser through request interception. The finding's userImpact ('told, silently, that there are none') is true of the PAYLOAD and false of the PAGE, which is the surface the impact claim is made about. What is genuinely wrong is the banner's DIAGNOSIS - it tells a manager holding 58 players in a 58-slot league that his roster 'has no clear positional surplus', because rosterAnalysis was computed on the 10 assets that survived the gate. That is a misattributed cause shown to the user, which is a P1 defect, not silence. (2) The finding omits the mitigation and the residue: /settings exposes ktcSuggestionTopN (frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:536-541, default 150, forwarded at frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:1544-1545, clamped to [50,300] at server.py:6046-6052), so a user can rescue 5 of the 8 teams; and 4 teams (Ty, Kich, jstuedle, Blaine) still return zero at the slider's maximum, so the gate is not the whole story for them - surplusPositions stays [] even with a 300-asset pool.

correctedBlastRadius.note: blast radius as stated is right; severity is not. A warning banner plus a matched-count is rendered on /trade, and /settings exposes a slider that raises the gate to 300.

whatWouldSettleIt: Nothing further - reproduced exactly and the causal test is decisive. If anyone wants to restore P0 they must show a page state where a WRONG number is displayed with no warning; the empty-feed state shows both a count and a banner.

FIT-COORDINATE CHECK (scripts/fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:123-148, 201-207, 370-372): the IDP master is fit on _load_idptc_idp_values() - the IDP-ONLY slice - with p = i/(n-1) over THAT slice and values renormalised values[i]/top*9999. BLAST-RADIUS RECOUNT: DL/LB/DB rows in the contract = 398, but rows actually carrying at least one of the four IDP rank-signal sources = 281. The other 117 IDP rows carry only anchors and cannot be moved by this mechanism.

COUNTERFACTUAL ON THE FINAL VALUE (re-blend with the same alpha=0.10 hierarchical rule, IDP-scope contributions replaced by GLOBAL-master values at the identical stamped percentile; reconstruction validates at median 0.06% error vs stamped rankDerivedValue): median +8.94%, p90 +42.1%, max +135.7%; 263/281 rows move >5%.
reasoning: The observation is exactly right and the mechanism is real: an IDP-only source's rank is ladder-translated into combined-pool coordinates (registry comment at data_contract.py:1159-1171 says so explicitly), the percentile denominator is the combined-pool 500, and _curve_for_source (data_contract.py:6888-6894) then routes on `scope` to a curve fit on IDP-only percentiles. Feeding combined-pool p into an IDP-slice-fit curve is a genuine units error and I verified it to the digit. Three things are overstated. (1) The reproduction command does not run as published - repro_blend.py computes none of the cited ratios and no generator for them is archived, which violates protocol rule 1. The numbers survive only because I rebuilt the measurement myself. (2) blastRadius.playersAffected=398 is the count of ALL DL/LB/DB rows, not the affected ones. Only 281 rows carry an IDP rank-signal vote; 398 overstates it by 42%. (3) requiredRepair ('route to GLOBAL; re-fit is not required') is not supported by the finding's own evidence and I found a second scale defect it does not name. Its correctness criterion is ratio ~= 1.0, and the GLOBAL counterfactual returns per-source medians of 0.92, 0.92, 1.29 and 1.32 - a wider spread than the offense control band it is compared against. Worse: _percentile_pairs renormalises the IDP slice so the best IDP = 9999, but on the live board the best IDP's anchor value is 6444 (Hutchinson), so the IDP master is fit in units 1.552x the scale its output is consumed in. Correct-coordinate IDP routing would therefore ALSO be wrong, by +55% at the top; the combined-pool percentile injection is currently deflating an over-scaled curve back toward the anchor, which is why Hutchinson lands at 0.873 of the anchor rather than 1.552. Two defects are compounding here, not one, and the naive re-route the finding prescribes moves the affected IDP rows up a median 8.9% (p90 42%) with no validation that the new numbers are right. Priority P1 is honest and unchanged; the alpha=0.10 IDP shrinkage damps the top of the board hard (Hutchinson rankDerivedValue 6362 vs anchor 6444, 1.3%) and the large moves are concentrated in the deep tail where the IDP master and GLOBAL diverge most (663 vs 1808 at p=0.9).

correctedBlastRadius.note: 398 counts every DL/LB/DB row; 117 of those carry only anchor sources and are untouched by this mechanism.

whatWouldSettleIt: Archive the script that produced .idpCurveScaleMismatch so the published command runs. To settle the REPAIR (which this verdict does not endorse): re-fit the IDP master on the combined-pool percentile the ladder actually emits AND on the anchor's un-renormalised IDP values (top 6444, not 9999), then re-measure the per-source ratio band against the offense control; a fix is only proven when both the median lands near 1.0 and the spread narrows to the offense band, which routing to GLOBAL alone does not achieve.
